summary: planDependentSync (internal/cli/sync.go) no longer calls db.SaveSyncState itself for --full's resume-offset tracking; it only records where the batch STARTS (dependentSyncPlan.fullOffsetKey/fullOffsetBase) and returns that alongside the plan. runDependentFanOut persists the advanced offset after the fetch/store loop actually completes, advancing only by the number of LEADING ids (in plan.ids' deterministic sort order) that succeeded -- not a raw success count (which could wrongly skip a scattered failure in the middle of the batch) and not "only if the whole batch succeeded" (which would let one chronically-failing id anywhere in the window pin the offset, and therefore the rest of the pass behind it, forever). failedIDs, a map populated by both failure sites in the fan-out worker pool, is walked in plan.ids' original order after the loop to compute this. Any future dependent that adds --full offset tracking must persist through this same plan-then-advance-by-verified-prefix shape, not call SaveSyncState during planning and not gate advancement on a simple failure count.
reason: Found by Greptile's automated review on the upstream PR splitting this branch's work (mvanhorn/printing-press-library#1773 and #1774), across two review rounds on the same mechanism. Round 1: the original implementation advanced the durable full-progress offset for every planned parent id before a single network or store operation ran, so a transient failure partway through a bounded batch left the failed record's dependent data missing or stale until the entire multi-call pass wrapped around. Round 2, after the first fix (gate advancement on zero failures in the batch): Greptile correctly identified that this traded one bug for another -- a parent that fails CONSISTENTLY (not just once) would then permanently pin the offset at the start of its window, blocking every other id in that window and every window after it in the pass, indefinitely, even though most of the batch keeps succeeding on every retry.
validated_outcome: go build/vet/test and verify_skill.py all green (govulncheck not run locally, no dependency changes). Three end-to-end regression tests drive the real fetch/store path (not planDependentSync in isolation, which can't observe fetch failures): TestFullSyncOffsetDoesNotAdvancePastAPartialBatchFailure (a failure at the START of a batch keeps the whole batch pending). TestFullSyncOffsetAdvancesPastLeadingSuccessesEvenWithATrailingFailure (a failure at the END of a batch still lets the offset advance past the leading successes, so the next call sees only the persistently-failing id, not the whole batch again -- proves the pass doesn't wedge). TestFullSyncOffsetStopsAtFirstFailureNotJustSuccessCount (a failure in the MIDDLE of a batch, with a later success, proves advancement stops at the first failure's position rather than using a raw success count that would skip past it). Also confirmed via `go test -race` scoped to every dependent-fan-out test that the new failedIDs map introduces no data race; a pre-existing, unrelated race in syncResource's shared event-stream writer (flat-resource worker pool, sync.go:557) was discovered incidentally by the same -race run and left untouched as out of scope for this fix.
